subject.title: [Feature]: Automatic Output Sanitization for Sensitive Data

question: Should OpenClaw own automatic final-output sensitive-data sanitization in core, expose it only through plugin hooks, or limit core to the current log/transcript/tool redaction boundaries?
rationale: The issue changes provider egress and user-visible output semantics, may require new config/defaults, and has security false-positive and false-negative tradeoffs that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Approve a narrow core design first
options.body: Define the protected output paths, default mode, reporting, opt-out behavior, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Route to plugin ownership
options.body: Keep core lean and document the reply/message hook path while tracking only missing hook or SDK gaps in core.

options.title: Keep current boundaries
options.body: Close or defer this request if maintainers decide log/transcript/tool-payload redaction is the intended core scope for now.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow core design first
recommendation.body: Define the protected output paths, default mode, reporting, opt-out behavior, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This group best matches the security boundary, defaults, and sensitive-data handling decision.
